q: The City & Guilds 2382 18th Edition exam is:
why: It's open book — your copy of BS 7671 plus a calculator — 60 questions, 2 hours.
answerText: Open book, 60 questions, 2 hours

q: What is the typical minimum pass mark, and the score you should really be aiming for?
why: Pass marks can vary slightly by cohort — treat 60% as the floor and aim well above it.

q: Because the exam is open-book, your revision time is best spent:
options: Memorising every table value word for word
Learning the structure of the book and practising finding the right clause/table quickly
why: The real skill tested is fast, accurate navigation and application — not rote recall.
answerText: Learning the structure of the book and practising finding the right clause/table quickly

q: If a question gives you numerical data, the safest approach is:
options: Guess based on similar past questions
Work the calculation through methodically using the correct formula and reference
Skip and never return to it
answerText: Work the calculation through methodically using the correct formula and reference

q: Which item is essential to bring to the exam alongside ID?
options: The current edition of BS 7671 and a scientific calculator
A copy of the On-Site Guide only
why: Check your exam centre's exact permitted-materials list beforehand — some restrict which additional guides are allowed.
answerText: The current edition of BS 7671 and a scientific calculator

q: "Basic protection" refers to protection against electric shock:
why: Fault protection is the single-fault-condition case (ADS, earthing, bonding).
answerText: Under normal, fault-free conditions

q: What does "Zs" represent?
options: The impedance of the earth electrode only
The total earth fault loop impedance (external + internal)
The resistance of the line conductor only
why: Zs = Ze + (R1 + R2).
answerText: The total earth fault loop impedance (external + internal)

q: PME stands for:
why: PME describes a TN-C-S supply where the combined PEN conductor is earthed at multiple points by the DNO.
answerText: Protective Multiple Earthing

q: In a TT earthing system, the installation's means of earthing is provided by:
options: A PEN conductor from the DNO
Bonding to gas and water pipes only
answerText: A local earth electrode

q: SELV is defined as:
options: A system not exceeding 50V a.c., electrically separated from earth and other systems
Any circuit protected by an RCD
A circuit with a functional earth connection
answerText: A system not exceeding 50V a.c., electrically separated from earth and other systems

q: "Prospective fault current" (PFC) is:
options: The current that would flow for a fault of negligible impedance
The maximum current a cable can carry continuously
The rated current of the protective device
The design current of the circuit
answerText: The current that would flow for a fault of negligible impedance

q: A "competent person" under BS 7671 is someone who:
options: Holds a City & Guilds 2382 certificate only
Has the skill, knowledge and experience to avoid danger to themselves and others
Has more than 10 years' experience regardless of training
answerText: Has the skill, knowledge and experience to avoid danger to themselves and others

q: The term "exposed-conductive-part" describes:
options: A touchable conductive part, not normally live, that can become live under fault conditions
Any conductive part of the installation, live or not
A live conductor with damaged insulation
answerText: A touchable conductive part, not normally live, that can become live under fault conditions

q: An "extraneous-conductive-part" is:
options: A conductive part liable to introduce a potential, not forming part of the electrical installation (e.g. structural steel)
answerText: A conductive part liable to introduce a potential, not forming part of the electrical installation (e.g. structural steel)

q: What is a "circuit protective conductor" (cpc)?
options: The conductor connecting exposed-conductive-parts to the main earthing terminal
The line conductor of a final circuit
A conductor used only for functional earthing
answerText: The conductor connecting exposed-conductive-parts to the main earthing terminal

q: RCBO is an abbreviation for:
options: A device combining overcurrent and residual current protection in one unit
answerText: A device combining overcurrent and residual current protection in one unit

q: "Diversity" in an electrical installation refers to:
options: The requirement to use different cable types on every circuit
The allowance made because not all connected loads run simultaneously at full demand
answerText: The allowance made because not all connected loads run simultaneously at full demand

q: Part 3 (Assessment of General Characteristics) requires the designer to consider all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Purpose, supplies and structure of the installation
The exact make and model of every light fitting
answerText: The exact make and model of every light fitting

q: "External influences", coded AA/AB/AC..., relate to:
options: The financial cost of the installation
Environmental conditions affecting equipment selection (temperature, altitude, water, impact)
answerText: Environmental conditions affecting equipment selection (temperature, altitude, water, impact)

q: Before working on an existing installation, BS 7671 requires assessment of:
options: Supply/installation characteristics likely to affect the design, including maximum demand, earthing arrangement, and condition of equipment to be reused
The colour of existing cables only
answerText: Supply/installation characteristics likely to affect the design, including maximum demand, earthing arrangement, and condition of equipment to be reused

q: Maximum demand of an installation is assessed:
options: By adding the rated current of every appliance with no allowance
Taking diversity into account, using recognised guidance
It is not required under Part 3
answerText: Taking diversity into account, using recognised guidance

q: Compatibility (Part 3) requires checking that:
options: All equipment is the same colour
Equipment characteristics (starting current, harmonics, leakage) won't harmfully affect other equipment or the supply
All circuits use the same device rating
answerText: Equipment characteristics (starting current, harmonics, leakage) won't harmfully affect other equipment or the supply

q: Which is an example of "AD" (presence of water) external-influence classification?
answerText: AD4 – splashing

q: For a TN system, the maximum disconnection time for a final circuit ≤32A is:
For a TT system, the maximum disconnection time for a final circuit ≤32A is:
For distribution circuits (and final circuits >32A) on a TN system, the maximum disconnection time is:
answerText: 5s

q: Additional protection by a 30mA RCD (411.3.3) is required for socket outlets ≤32A for use by ordinary persons:
options: In all locations, with only very limited listed exceptions
answerText: In all locations, with only very limited listed exceptions

q: In domestic premises, 30mA RCD additional protection is also specifically required for:
why: Regulation 411.3.4 extended the requirement to domestic lighting circuits.
answerText: AC final circuits supplying luminaires (lighting)

q: Fault protection (single-fault-condition shock protection) is most commonly achieved by:
answerText: Automatic Disconnection of Supply (ADS)

q: Electrical separation (413) as a protective measure relies on:
options: A single circuit from an isolating source, live parts not connected to earth or another circuit
answerText: A single circuit from an isolating source, live parts not connected to earth or another circuit

q: SELV and PELV are protective measures classed under:
options: Extra-low voltage (both basic and fault protection from the low voltage itself)
Obstacles and placing out of reach
answerText: Extra-low voltage (both basic and fault protection from the low voltage itself)

q: The nominal voltage limit for SELV/PELV under normal conditions is:
answerText: 50V a.c. / 120V ripple-free d.c.

q: "Obstacles" and "placing out of reach" as protective measures are:
options: Permitted for ordinary persons in all installations
Only permitted where supervised/controlled by skilled or instructed persons
answerText: Only permitted where supervised/controlled by skilled or instructed persons

q: Basic protection by insulation of live parts requires the insulation to:
options: Be removable with a standard tool for maintenance
Only be removable by destruction, solvents or heat — not by hand
Be any colour so long as present
answerText: Only be removable by destruction, solvents or heat — not by hand

q: A barrier providing basic protection must give at least a degree of protection of:
options: IPXXB (IP2X), or IPXXD on accessible horizontal top surfaces where required
answerText: IPXXB (IP2X), or IPXXD on accessible horizontal top surfaces where required

q: Which is correct about RCDs and TT systems?
options: An RCD is never required on TT if Zs is low enough
Because Ze is often too high for overcurrent devices alone, an RCD is almost always essential for fault protection
TT systems don't require an earth electrode
answerText: Because Ze is often too high for overcurrent devices alone, an RCD is almost always essential for fault protection

q: To confirm automatic disconnection will occur in time on a TN system, you must check:
options: That Zs does not exceed the tabulated maximum for that device and disconnection time
answerText: That Zs does not exceed the tabulated maximum for that device and disconnection time

q: Arc Fault Detection Devices (AFDDs) are designed to:
options: Detect arc faults that conventional overcurrent/RCD protection may miss, reducing fire risk
answerText: Detect arc faults that conventional overcurrent/RCD protection may miss, reducing fire risk

q: Under Regulation 421.1.7, AFDDs are required as a minimum for certain final circuits ≤32A in premises such as:
options: HMOs and similarly higher-risk residential premises listed in BS 7671
answerText: HMOs and similarly higher-risk residential premises listed in BS 7671

q: Where fitted, an AFDD should be installed:
options: At the furthest point of the circuit from the origin
At the origin of the final circuit it protects
In the socket outlet itself only
answerText: At the origin of the final circuit it protects

q: Regulation 422 deals with:
options: Precautions for locations with particular risks — fire, explosion, escape routes, high fire load
answerText: Precautions for locations with particular risks — fire, explosion, escape routes, high fire load

q: For a luminaire close to combustible material rated over 300W up to 500W, minimum spacing guidance is broadly around:
why: Illustrative bands: ≤100W≈0.5m, >100–300W≈0.8m, >300–500W≈1.0m — confirm current figures.

q: A "significant quantity" of flammable liquid, for fire-risk assessment purposes, is generally taken as:
answerText: 25 litres

q: Where a circuit passes through a fire-risk location (e.g. escape route), measures may include:
options: Ignoring the risk if PVC insulated
Fire-resistant wiring systems, avoiding combustible surfaces, protection against mechanical damage
No special measures are ever needed
answerText: Fire-resistant wiring systems, avoiding combustible surfaces, protection against mechanical damage

q: Thermal effects requirements (Chapter 42) primarily protect against:
options: Burns and fire from heat generated by equipment or faults
answerText: Burns and fire from heat generated by equipment or faults

q: Fixed equipment likely to reach ignition temperatures should be:
options: Positioned/guarded so adjacent materials can't reach a dangerous temperature, or mounted/enclosed to withstand it
answerText: Positioned/guarded so adjacent materials can't reach a dangerous temperature, or mounted/enclosed to withstand it

q: For hand-held equipment, the maximum accessible temperature for non-metallic parts liable to be touched is around:
The basic rule for selecting a protective device against overload (433.1) is:
options: Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz, and I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz
Ib has no relationship to Iz
answerText: Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz, and I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz

q: "Ib" represents:
options: The rated current of the protective device
The design current of the circuit
The tabulated current-carrying capacity of the cable
The breaking capacity of the device
answerText: The design current of the circuit

q: "Iz" represents:
options: The rated current of the device
The cable's effective current-carrying capacity in its installed conditions
answerText: The cable's effective current-carrying capacity in its installed conditions

q: The adiabatic equation for a conductor's thermal withstand under fault is:
answerText: S = √(I²t) / k

q: Using S=√(I²t)/k, for I=1000A, t=0.4s, k=115, the minimum csa is approximately:
answerText: 5.5 mm²

q: The breaking capacity of a protective device must be:
options: Less than the prospective fault current at that point
Equal to or greater than the prospective fault current at that point (or backed up per 434.5.1)
Ignored if an RCD is fitted
answerText: Equal to or greater than the prospective fault current at that point (or backed up per 434.5.1)

q: A "distribution circuit" (as opposed to a final circuit) is one that:
options: Connects the origin (or a distribution board) to another board/consumer unit supplying final circuits
answerText: Connects the origin (or a distribution board) to another board/consumer unit supplying final circuits

q: Overload protection may be omitted (433.3) only where, for example:
options: Consequences of overload are negligible/unlikely, under the specific conditions BS 7671 lists
Never — overload protection is always mandatory with no exceptions
The customer requests it in writing
answerText: Consequences of overload are negligible/unlikely, under the specific conditions BS 7671 lists

q: Table 43.1 provides:
options: k-values for the adiabatic equation by conductor/insulation/joint
answerText: k-values for the adiabatic equation by conductor/insulation/joint

q: For a tinned soldered joint in copper with 60°C thermosetting insulation, a commonly referenced k-value example is around:
why: Exact k-values depend on the specific combination — confirm against the current Table 43.1.

q: Surge Protective Devices (SPDs) protect against:
answerText: Transient overvoltages (e.g. lightning, switching events)

q: A risk assessment (or the simplified method) determines:
options: Whether SPDs are required for a given installation
The size of the consumer unit only
answerText: Whether SPDs are required for a given installation

q: A mechanical maintenance switch (537.3.2.4) must be capable of:
options: Being secured OFF (locking, or removal of a fuse/link) to prevent unintended reclosure
answerText: Being secured OFF (locking, or removal of a fuse/link) to prevent unintended reclosure

q: A means of isolation must:
options: Never be needed if an RCD is fitted
Disconnect all live supply conductors of the relevant part, and be identifiable and accessible
Only be fitted at the main switchboard
answerText: Disconnect all live supply conductors of the relevant part, and be identifiable and accessible

q: A functional switch (e.g. a light switch) is used to:
options: Control normal operation without necessarily disconnecting all poles
answerText: Control normal operation without necessarily disconnecting all poles

q: Emergency switching devices must operate:
options: Rapidly, by a single action, to remove danger
Only when the RCD also trips
answerText: Rapidly, by a single action, to remove danger

q: A switch used for isolation should be installed so that it:
options: Cannot be inadvertently or accidentally operated by unauthorised persons while isolated
answerText: Cannot be inadvertently or accidentally operated by unauthorised persons while isolated

q: Firefighter's switches (e.g. for discharge-tube signage) are typically:
options: Coloured red, accessible to the fire service, with an indicator lamp
Located inside a locked switch room only
answerText: Coloured red, accessible to the fire service, with an indicator lamp

q: BS EN 61439-6 relates to:
answerText: Busbar trunking systems

q: A cable's current-carrying capacity (Iz) is derived from the tabulated value (It) by applying:
options: Rating factors for ambient temperature, grouping, thermal insulation etc.
Only the length of the cable
answerText: Rating factors for ambient temperature, grouping, thermal insulation etc.

q: A cable in an ambient temperature above the tabulated reference has its capacity:
options: Reduced, via an ambient temperature factor (Ca) less than 1
answerText: Reduced, via an ambient temperature factor (Ca) less than 1

q: A grouping rating factor (Cg) is applied because:
options: Grouped cables mutually heat each other, reducing safe current per cable
answerText: Grouped cables mutually heat each other, reducing safe current per cable

q: A cable fully surrounded by thermal insulation has its capacity:
options: Increased, since insulation retains heat usefully
Significantly reduced — a thermal insulation factor (Ci) less than 1 applies
answerText: Significantly reduced — a thermal insulation factor (Ci) less than 1 applies

q: For a 90°C cable at reference ambient 30°C, installed at 40°C, Ca is calculated using:
answerText: Ca = √[(θz−θa)/(θz−θref)]

q: The recommended maximum voltage drop, origin to load point, for a low-voltage public supply, is generally:
answerText: 3% for lighting, 5% for other uses

q: Voltage drop in a cable run is approximately calculated using:
options: It can only be measured, not calculated
answerText: mV/A/m × Ib × length(m) / 1000

q: Using mV/A/m=18, Ib=20A, length=15m, the approximate voltage drop is:
The minimum copper line conductor csa generally quoted for a fixed power circuit is:
why: 1.5mm² is typical for lighting; 2.5mm² is the common general minimum for power — always check the specific circuit and exceptions.
answerText: 2.5 mm²

q: A cable through a timber joist, outside a permitted safe zone, must (522.6.201) be:
options: At least 50mm from the top/bottom of the joist, or otherwise protected against damage
answerText: At least 50mm from the top/bottom of the joist, or otherwise protected against damage

q: A cable in a wall at less than 50mm depth, outside a safe zone, generally requires:
options: Additional protection, typically 30mA RCD or robust mechanical protection
answerText: Additional protection, typically 30mA RCD or robust mechanical protection

q: Safe zones for cables in walls are generally defined as bands:
options: Within 150mm of a wall/ceiling junction or corner, or running directly to/from an accessory
Only at the centre of the wall
There are no defined safe zones
answerText: Within 150mm of a wall/ceiling junction or corner, or running directly to/from an accessory

q: For a single-phase a.c. installation, the line conductor core colour is:
answerText: Brown

q: The protective (earth) conductor is identified by:
answerText: Green-and-yellow bi-colour combination

q: For a DC circuit, the colour identification for the positive conductor (L+) is:
why: DC positive is Brown; DC negative is Grey.
answerText: Brown

q: In a TN-S system, the earth path back to source is provided by:
options: A separate local earth electrode only
The metallic sheath/armour of the supply cable
answerText: The metallic sheath/armour of the supply cable

q: In a TN-C-S system, within the installation the neutral and protective functions are:
options: Combined only on the supply side (PEN); separated into N and cpc within the installation
answerText: Combined only on the supply side (PEN); separated into N and cpc within the installation

q: Main protective bonding connects extraneous-conductive-parts to:
answerText: The main earthing terminal

q: The minimum copper-equivalent csa for main protective bonding per Table 54.8 is:
why: 6mm² is the BS 7671 table minimum, though DNOs often specify 10mm² in practice on PME supplies.
answerText: 6 mm²

q: Supplementary bonding conductors NOT mechanically protected need a minimum csa of:
answerText: 4 mm²

q: Supplementary bonding conductors that ARE mechanically protected need a minimum csa of:
answerText: 2.5 mm²

q: A warning notice at a bonding connection should read:
answerText: "Safety Electrical Connection – Do Not Remove"

q: Zs = Ze + (R1+R2) means:
options: Zs is independent of the circuit's protective conductor resistance
Total loop impedance = external impedance + line and cpc resistance within the circuit
R1 and R2 refer to two separate earth electrodes
Ze is measured after the circuit is wired
answerText: Total loop impedance = external impedance + line and cpc resistance within the circuit

q: Which system relies on the general mass of earth rather than a metallic path back to the source?
options: None — all use a local electrode
answerText: TT

q: A PEN conductor is:
options: A conductor combining protective conductor and neutral functions, used by the DNO in PME systems
A type of bonding conductor only
A conductor used exclusively in SELV circuits
answerText: A conductor combining protective conductor and neutral functions, used by the DNO in PME systems

q: Under an "open PEN" fault on a PME supply, exposed-conductive-parts can become:
options: Live at a dangerous voltage relative to true earth
Automatically disconnected instantly with no further action
answerText: Live at a dangerous voltage relative to true earth

q: Which is generally NOT acceptable as the sole means of earthing for a TT installation?
options: An earth mat or plate electrode
Reliance on the metallic water service pipe alone
A properly designed earth electrode system
answerText: Reliance on the metallic water service pipe alone

q: Bonding of simultaneously-accessible exposed and extraneous parts, beyond main bonding, is called:
answerText: Supplementary (equipotential) bonding

q: Functional earthing (Section 545, revised by A4) is provided:
options: For correct equipment operation and EMC, distinct from protective earthing
Instead of protective earthing, replacing it
answerText: For correct equipment operation and EMC, distinct from protective earthing

q: Initial verification of a new installation comprises:
options: Inspection followed by testing (dead tests, then live tests)
A visual check by the customer
answerText: Inspection followed by testing (dead tests, then live tests)

q: Which test is normally carried out FIRST in the dead-test sequence?
answerText: Continuity of protective conductors (incl. bonding)

q: A ring final circuit continuity test (figure-of-eight method) confirms:
options: No breaks or crossed connections in the ring, and correct polarity at each outlet
answerText: No breaks or crossed connections in the ring, and correct polarity at each outlet

q: Insulation resistance testing on a circuit up to 500V is typically carried out at:
answerText: 500V DC, minimum 1.0 MΩ

q: For SELV/PELV circuits, insulation resistance testing is typically carried out at:
answerText: 250V DC, minimum 0.5 MΩ

q: Before insulation resistance testing, you should typically:
options: Disconnect/isolate voltage-sensitive electronics that could be damaged by the test voltage
Switch all RCDs to test position
answerText: Disconnect/isolate voltage-sensitive electronics that could be damaged by the test voltage

q: Polarity verification confirms that:
options: Single-pole devices switch the line conductor, and lampholder centre-pins connect to line not neutral
The RCD trips within the correct time
answerText: Single-pole devices switch the line conductor, and lampholder centre-pins connect to line not neutral

q: Ze (external earth fault loop impedance) is measured:
options: With main switch closed, main bonding in place, and the earthing conductor temporarily disconnected from the MET
It cannot be measured, only calculated
answerText: With main switch closed, main bonding in place, and the earthing conductor temporarily disconnected from the MET

q: A general-purpose RCD tested at its rated residual current (IΔn) should disconnect within:
answerText: 300ms

q: The same RCD, tested at 5×IΔn, should disconnect within:
answerText: 40ms

q: An Electrical Installation Certificate (EIC) is used for:
options: Periodic inspection of an existing installation
New installation work, or an addition/alteration including a new circuit
Minor alterations not involving a new circuit
answerText: New installation work, or an addition/alteration including a new circuit

q: A Minor Electrical Installation Works Certificate is appropriate for:
options: Additions/alterations that do NOT include a new circuit
answerText: Additions/alterations that do NOT include a new circuit

q: An Electrical Installation Condition Report (EICR) is used to:
options: Report on the condition of an existing installation following periodic inspection
Replace the need for an EIC on new work
answerText: Report on the condition of an existing installation following periodic inspection

q: Observation code "C1" on an EICR means:
options: Potentially dangerous — urgent remedial action required
Danger present — immediate remedial action required
answerText: Danger present — immediate remedial action required

q: Observation code "C2" on an EICR means:
options: Potentially dangerous — urgent remedial action required
answerText: Potentially dangerous — urgent remedial action required

q: Observation code "FI" on an EICR indicates:
answerText: Further investigation required without delay

q: The typical maximum recommended interval before the next EICR for an owner-occupied domestic dwelling is generally:
options: 10 years, or at change of occupancy
answerText: 10 years, or at change of occupancy

q: Under the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector Regulations, landlords in England must have an EICR at intervals not exceeding:
answerText: 5 years, or sooner as required

q: In a bathroom (701), Zone 0 is defined as:
options: The area more than 3m from the bath
The interior of the bath tub or shower basin itself
Only the area under the sink
answerText: The interior of the bath tub or shower basin itself

q: Zone 1 in a bathroom extends broadly to:
options: Above zone 0 up to 2.25m from the floor, within the bath/shower boundary
answerText: Above zone 0 up to 2.25m from the floor, within the bath/shower boundary

q: The minimum IP rating required for equipment in Zone 0 of a bathroom is:
answerText: IPX7

q: Supplementary bonding in a bathroom may be omitted, provided (among other conditions):
options: All final circuits meet 411.3.2 disconnection times, have 30mA RCD protection, and main bonding is in place
answerText: All final circuits meet 411.3.2 disconnection times, have 30mA RCD protection, and main bonding is in place

q: In a swimming pool location (702), Zone 0 covers:
options: The interior of the pool basin
answerText: The interior of the pool basin

q: For a pool with a diving board, Zone 1 typically extends vertically above the board to around:
In a sauna (703), Zone 1 is generally the space:
options: From floor level up to around 1.0m, near the heater
answerText: From floor level up to around 1.0m, near the heater

q: Sauna Zone 3 generally starts:
options: There is no Zone 3 in saunas
answerText: Above around the 1.0m mark

q: Construction sites (704) typically use 110V CTE for portable tools because:
options: It looks different from permanent supplies
It halves the shock voltage to earth (55V) in harsh, damp conditions
BS 7671 does not address construction sites
answerText: It halves the shock voltage to earth (55V) in harsh, damp conditions

q: Agricultural/horticultural premises (705) require additional RCD protection because:
options: Livestock can be more sensitive to shock, and the environment is damp/corrosive
Section 705 only applies to arable farms
answerText: Livestock can be more sensitive to shock, and the environment is damp/corrosive

q: A caravan pitch electrical supply (708) is typically provided via:
options: A hardwired connection with no plug
A weatherproof socket-outlet per pitch (commonly 16A), individually RCD-protected
A 13A domestic socket with no RCD
answerText: A weatherproof socket-outlet per pitch (commonly 16A), individually RCD-protected

q: The flexible cable connecting a caravan to its pitch supply should have a minimum csa of around:
answerText: 2.5 mm²

q: Marina (709) socket-outlets supplying pontoons/berths should be:
options: Standard sockets with no special consideration
Individually 30mA RCD-protected, suitably rated for the marine environment
Fed from a single shared unprotected circuit
answerText: Individually 30mA RCD-protected, suitably rated for the marine environment

q: Medical locations (710) often use an IT system in higher-risk 'Group 2' areas primarily because:
options: A first fault doesn't force immediate disconnection, so life-support equipment can keep running
It removes the need for any earthing
IT systems are mandatory in all medical rooms
answerText: A first fault doesn't force immediate disconnection, so life-support equipment can keep running

q: Amendment 4 revised Section 710 (medical locations) primarily around:
options: Removing the requirement for supplementary bonding entirely
Enhanced supplementary bonding procedures and a schedule for recording resistance measurements
answerText: Enhanced supplementary bonding procedures and a schedule for recording resistance measurements

q: Solar PV (712) DC-side installations need particular care because:
options: DC arcs can be harder to extinguish, and can't be switched off at will while illuminated
DC has no associated shock risk
There is no specific PV guidance in BS 7671
answerText: DC arcs can be harder to extinguish, and can't be switched off at will while illuminated

q: For EV charging (722) on a PME supply, a key safety concern is:
options: Open-PEN fault risk making vehicle metalwork dangerously live — addressed by open-PEN detection or a TT arrangement
PME supplies need no special measures for EV charging
answerText: Open-PEN fault risk making vehicle metalwork dangerously live — addressed by open-PEN detection or a TT arrangement

q: RCD protection for an EV charge point commonly addresses smooth DC leakage by using:
options: A Type B RCD, or Type A plus a 6mA DC RDC-DD
answerText: A Type B RCD, or Type A plus a 6mA DC RDC-DD

q: Temporary installations at exhibitions/fairgrounds require:
options: No RCD protection because they're temporary
30mA RCD protection on socket-outlet/public-accessible circuits, equipment out of arm's reach where relevant
answerText: 30mA RCD protection on socket-outlet/public-accessible circuits, equipment out of arm's reach where relevant

q: Restrictive conductive locations (706), e.g. inside a metal tank, impose extra precautions mainly because:
options: Body resistance is effectively reduced by extensive contact with earthed metal, raising shock risk
There is no additional risk in confined metal spaces
It only relates to gas installations
answerText: Body resistance is effectively reduced by extensive contact with earthed metal, raising shock risk

q: A prosumer's low-voltage installation (Part 8) is one that:
options: Both consumes AND can generate/store/potentially export electricity
Has no connection to the public supply
Is only found in industrial premises
answerText: Both consumes AND can generate/store/potentially export electricity

q: An EEMS (Electrical Energy Management System) is used to:
options: Monitor and control generation, storage and consumption, potentially including automatic disconnection
answerText: Monitor and control generation, storage and consumption, potentially including automatic disconnection

q: A PEI (Power Electronic Interface, e.g. a PV/battery inverter) needs a suitable means of earthing in island mode because:
options: When disconnected from the DNO, the normal PME earth reference is unavailable, so an alternative is needed
Earthing is never required for inverters
It only applies to three-phase inverters
answerText: When disconnected from the DNO, the normal PME earth reference is unavailable, so an alternative is needed

q: Amendment 4 introduced a completely new Chapter 57 covering:
options: Stationary secondary batteries (BESS) — siting, ventilation, fire risk, isolation
answerText: Stationary secondary batteries (BESS) — siting, ventilation, fire risk, isolation

q: Amendment 4 introduced a new Section 716, addressing:
options: Power over Ethernet — thermal/derating where data cables carry DC power
answerText: Power over Ethernet — thermal/derating where data cables carry DC power

q: Amendment 4 introduced a new Chapter 81 covering:
options: An energy-efficiency assessment framework for LV installations
answerText: An energy-efficiency assessment framework for LV installations

q: BS 7671 Amendment 4:2026 was published on:
answerText: 15 April 2026

q: Chapter 57 guidance generally advises stationary secondary batteries should NOT be sited:
options: In roof spaces, due to detection, ventilation and fire-containment challenges
answerText: In roof spaces, due to detection, ventilation and fire-containment challenges

q: Which of these originates from Amendment 2:2022 rather than Amendment 4:2026?
